tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — THREE BLUESTEMS, NOT ONE
tiles.details: Trace a complete mature flowering culm and locate the narrow sheath (spathe) surrounding each flowering raceme pair. This is a separately accepted Anatherum species historically called Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus, not automatically true bushy bluestem (A. glomeratum). The current Linda Jo Conn image and Starr historical-variety images teach gross habit only. Do not certify the source photo or a Hays occurrence as this species from a fluffy head. Gallery 0 is the sole source-labelled original flowering image; panels 1, 4 and 5 are historical var. pumilus source views, not independent modern vouchers or measured anatomy.
tiles.short: Silky spathe-enclosed paired racemes are only a starting clue; this species needs measured parts.
tiles.status: PROVISIONAL — SPECIES ID NOT VERIFIED FROM GROSS PHOTOS

tiles.heading: 02 · TOUCH AND MEASURE THE UPPER SHEATH
tiles.details: Wipff and Shaw's Texas-authored 2018 key contrasts A. tenuispatheum's mostly smooth upper leaf sheaths and narrow raceme-enclosing sheath, typically less than 2.5 mm wide, with A. eremicum's often scabrous upper sheath and wider, often over 2.5 mm enclosing sheath. Measure a mature attached enclosing sheath perpendicular to its width, with a 1-mm bar; the published tendencies are not absolute cutoffs. No existing photo proves this texture or width.
tiles.short: Published key: upper sheaths generally smooth; raceme-enclosing sheath often under 2.5 mm wide.

tiles.heading: 03 · FIND THE TRUE MEMBRANOUS LIGULE
tiles.details: Open the inner blade/sheath collar at 10–20× and measure the actual membranous ligule, not adjacent throat hairs or a folded leaf blade. The published tenuispatheum condition is a membrane less than 1 mm with relatively long marginal cilia; A. eremicum more often has a 1–2 mm membrane with shorter cilia. Both structure and scale must be visible on the same authenticated specimen. Existing habit photos cannot demonstrate either condition.
tiles.short: True ligule membrane usually under 1 mm with long marginal cilia.
tiles.status: PUBLISHED MEASUREMENT — TRUE COLLAR MACRO MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · SESSILE SPIKELET, GLUMES, LEMMA AND AWN
tiles.details: At 10–20× photograph one intact sessile/pedicellate spikelet pair still attached to a raceme joint with a 1-mm ruler. Identify the sessile fertile spikelet separately from its pedicellate partner, then expose the outer glumes and fertile lemma/palea to trace any awn to its true point of origin. Wipff and Shaw contrast a typically <3.8 mm sessile spikelet here with >4.2 mm in A. eremicum; overlapping or damaged material must remain undetermined. No independent glume, lemma, or awn dimensions are certified from the current photographs.
tiles.short: Published key: mature sessile spikelet usually under 3.8 mm; eremicum often over 4.2 mm.
tiles.status: MEASURED SPIKELET KEY — SAME-VOUCHER DISSECTION MISSING

tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES AND NAME TRAP
tiles.details: A. glomeratum generally has a dense brushlike terminal crown of many short silky racemes; A. virginicum more often has separated spathe-enclosed units. Neither gross pattern alone proves A. tenuispatheum. The especially important southwest comparison is separately accepted A. eremicum: use upper-sheath texture, enclosing-sheath width, true ligule and sessile spikelet together. Historical 'var. pumilus' photo labels and synonym spelling differences do not substitute for a modern voucher. Keep county-range status unchanged. For side-by-side gross habit, gallery 0 is the provisional target and galleries 2 (A. virginicum) and 3 (A. glomeratum) are explicitly DIFFERENT species; no authenticated A. eremicum photo is installed.
tiles.short: Separate bushy bluestem, broomsedge and southwestern A. eremicum.

tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY AND RIGHTS GATE
tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: taxonomist-verified mature flowering plant with attached upper sheaths, true ligule at 1-mm scale, enclosing raceme sheath width, a <3.8 mm candidate sessile spikelet with its pedicellate partner, separated glumes/lemma/palea/awn, and same-scale A. eremicum comparisons. NEEDS_SITE_QA: verify three existing source records, exact local JPEGs, Linda Jo Conn CC BY-NC terms and noncommercial eligibility, Starr CC BY attribution/adaptation, historical name and source-photo identity conflicts, two original gross arrows and provisional captions on the public site. Preserve taxonomy, county and source-photo holds; no invented fine arrows. The six panels comprise one Linda Jo Conn provisional source photo, three historical var. pumilus views and two DIFFERENT-species comparisons; do not count six panels as six diagnostic species photos.
tiles.short: PROVISIONAL_SPECIES_REPRODUCTIVE_ID_HOLD — do not mark this card finished.

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: ANATHERUM TENUISPATHEUM is an accepted distinct bluestem, old Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus 'ROBUST VARIANT', NOT the separate accepted Southwestern Anatherum eremicum (= var. scabriglumis). A published Texas-authored key supports typically SMOOTH sheaths, enclosing raceme sheath <2.5 mm, true ligule membrane <1 mm with LONG cilia, sessile spikelet <3.8 mm. Contrast eremicum's scabrous sheaths, >2.5 mm raceme sheath, 1–2 mm membrane with short cilia, >4.2 mm spikelets. The current archived source-labelled flowering photograph lacks a ruler, true ligule and spikelet macro: no ID hold clearance. Compare A. glomeratum and virginicum separately.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Wipff and Shaw's Texas-authored 2018 key contrasts A. tenuispatheum's mostly smooth upper leaf sheaths and narrow raceme-enclosing sheath, typically less than 2.5 mm wide, with A. eremicum's often scabrous upper sheath and wider, often over 2.5 mm enclosing sheath. Measure a mature attached enclosing sheath perpendicular to its width, with a 1-mm bar; the published tendencies are not absolute cutoffs. No existing photo proves this texture or width.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: At 10–20× photograph one intact sessile/pedicellate spikelet pair still attached to a raceme joint with a 1-mm ruler. Identify the sessile fertile spikelet separately from its pedicellate partner, then expose the outer glumes and fertile lemma/palea to trace any awn to its true point of origin. Wipff and Shaw contrast a typically <3.8 mm sessile spikelet here with >4.2 mm in A. eremicum; overlapping or damaged material must remain undetermined. No independent glume, lemma, or awn dimensions are certified from the current photographs.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.
